new_calendar.title: Personal Month-Grid Calendar (single-user desktop)

scenario.name: Personal Month-Grid Calendar (single-user desktop)
scenario.audience: A single local user on one machine who manages only their own appointments. No accounts, no sharing, no sync, no second calendar for anyone else.
scenario.objective: Create, read, edit, reschedule and delete your own titled appointments with a start and an end date-time in a fixed UTC+08:00 offset and optional location and notes, shown on a real seven-column month grid whose schedule is persisted locally across restarts and navigable back into past months.
workflow: Open the app: a month frame renders 7 weekday columns by 4-6 week rows for the current month, with a header showing the month and previous/next controls.
Double-click an empty day cell (or use the new-appointment action), type a title, set start and end date-time, optionally location and notes, then save.
The appointment appears as a block on the grid in every month its [start,end) span touches; overlapping appointments are all shown, never rejected.
Open the block, change title, time, location or notes, or reschedule it to another day and time; save and see the block move.
Use the header arrows to step to the next or previous month and again to return to a past month; the frame re-renders with that month's events.
Delete the appointment from the editor (probe-created records only) and confirm it disappears from the grid and the store.
Close and reopen the app: the appointments are still listed and navigating back to a past month still shows them.

capabilities: month-grid-frame: a single-window month frame of exactly 7 weekday columns by 4-6 week rows for the visible month, with a header that names the month and offers previous/next controls that move exactly one month (with year rollover) and re-render, including backwards into past months.

appointment-editor: an editor for one appointment carrying title, start date-time, end date-time and optional location and notes, which refuses a save whose end is not strictly after its start, or whose title is blank, and writes nothing on refusal.

span-and-overlap-rendering: each appointment is rendered as a block on every day its half-open [start,end) span touches, including across a month boundary, while overlapping appointments are shown side by side and never rejected.

edit-reschedule-delete: opening an existing block and changing its title, times, location or notes moves the block to the new slot, and deleting a record removes it from the grid and from the store while leaving other records untouched.
local-persistent-store: a single local JSON document per user holds the schedule, is written atomically, survives application restart, and is read back on launch without being rewritten.
limits: Only the month frame is implemented; there is no day, week, agenda or year view, and the upstream week-number toggle is deliberately not reproduced.
Rescheduling is done through the editor's date-time fields rather than by dragging a block to another day, so the upstream drag-and-drop reschedule is not reproduced.
The upstream Evolution Data Server / iCalendar source layer, calendar colours, calendars sidebar, context menus and libical interop are out of scope; the store is one local JSON document.
All instants use a fixed UTC+08:00 offset with no daylight-saving handling and no time-zone switch, so appointments do not follow a machine zone change.
There is no undo/redo, no search, no import/export, no recurring event, no all-day mode, no reminders, no attendee or invitation data.
The widget-tree half of the acceptance probe is reported as NOT_RUN on a machine without a graphical display; the model/store half still runs there.
The target code is not present in this workspace, so the probe is expected to fail loudly rather than pass until the implementation is written.
No upstream code was copied; the GPL-3.0 upstream project was read as a structural reference only.
